raw_response:
I am 72 years old this year. I have farmed these 9 mu in Quzhou County for 50 years. I only went to primary school, but I know my own fields better than any book. I watch what my neighbors do, and I only change if I saw it work on someone else's land first.

Last year my wheat made about 550 jin per mu and my maize made about 650 jin per mu. This year I will do almost the same thing. Change is risky, and a bad harvest is a disaster I cannot afford.

For winter wheat, I buy improved seed from the dealer in town — the same kind my neighbor Old Wang used last year. Before planting, I put one 50kg bag of compound fertilizer on every mu. That is 9 bags total for my whole farm. When the wheat greens up in March, I topdress with 25kg of urea per mu. I never cut back on fertilizer. Compound fertilizer is over 150 yuan a bag now, but if I use too little and the yield drops, I lose much more money. Wasting some fertilizer is just a cost; an empty table is a catastrophe. I irrigate three times from my well: once before winter if the soil is dry, once at jointing, and once at heading. The well pump costs electricity, but I cannot skip it. I spray herbicide once after the wheat emerges, and if I see aphids in spring, I spray insecticide once more. After the maize comes off in June, I rotary till the ground before planting wheat.

For summer maize, I plant hybrid seed right after wheat harvest, around June 10th. I have to hurry — if I plant after June 20th, everyone knows the yield falls. I put one 50kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting time, and when the maize grows to knee height — the big trumpet stage — I spread 20kg of urea per mu. That trumpet-stage topdressing is the most important. If you miss that, the ears do not fill properly. I irrigate twice: once when the seedlings are small if the rain does not come, and once at the big trumpet stage. I spray herbicide once after planting, and I spray insecticide once for corn borers. I do not till the land for maize. There is no time after wheat harvest — everyone here plants directly or uses no-tillage. That is how it is done.

I think about my whole budget. Nine bags of compound fertilizer for wheat, nine bags for maize, plus all that urea, plus seed, plus electricity for the well, plus pesticide — it adds up to thousands of yuan. My wife and I do all the labor ourselves. If harvest is very busy I might hire one person for one day, but I try to avoid paying wages. I would rather spend the money on fertilizer than lose yield. Old Wang tried to save money on fertilizer two years ago and his wheat was thin and yellow. I will not make that mistake.
